scope: How the public build commands build, package and flash an FP6 test image. Identity pins live in build-environment-fp6.json; this file holds no host paths.
notice_kind_reason: Android's licence classification for the extracted stock files; users extract them from Fairphone's own package. It grants no redistribution right.

avb.zero_header_reason: Generic kernel image v4 headers carry zero OS version and patch level; the versions live in the AVB properties, as on stock. The device configuration asks mkbootimg for zeros; the Android release tools that rebuild the images from target-files must keep them.

userdata.reason: As Fairphone's factory package: 4 MiB of zeros destroy the old filesystem, and first boot formats /data (formattable) with the phone's own size, encryption, casefolding and quota settings. A pre-formatted image would fix the size and features at build time.

metadata.label: metadata
metadata.reason: An empty f2fs filesystem of the metadata partition's size (stock metadata.img is the same size and type), made with the synced source's make_f2fs with a fixed UUID, time and seed so every build writes the same bytes.

frp.reason: As Fairphone's frp_for_factory.img: zeros with the last byte set, which clears factory reset protection and keeps OEM unlocking allowed. Byte-identical to the stock image.

misc.reason: As Fairphone's factory flash clears misc (the bootloader message, such as a pending recovery command), but by flashing zeros of the whole partition instead of fastboot erase. The size is the stock partition table's: 256 sectors of 4096 bytes in FP6.QREL.16.111.0; build package checks it against the factory package's partition table when that package is in the workspace.

shallow_prefetch.reason: The prebuilt projects with the largest depth-1 downloads, 2 to 8 GB each. Such a fetch from android.googlesource.com can break off; repo then fetches the project again without depth, which for these does not finish, and an interrupted sync leaves git directories repo later fetches with their whole history. build sync --shallow fetches these projects first, one revision each at depth 1, stops a transfer that stays below the speed limit and tries again a bounded number of times.
